regime: Pinned / negative gamma — fade the walls, respect the put wall on dips
headline: Fade rallies into the call walls — geopolitical risk and a hawkish Fed keep dealers pinned below the flip.
narrative: Sell strength into the call walls (SPX 7,700-7,730, SPY 770-772, QQQ 717-720) and buy dips toward the put walls, but keep size light since spot sits below each gamma flip in heavy negative gamma. Expect chop with downside skew — Middle East escalation and a hawkish Fed are the tape's drivers, not a clean trend, so don't chase either side hard.
why: Weekend US strikes near the Strait of Hormuz and Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks (lifting September hike odds) have pushed futures lower and yields/oil/dollar higher, and spot in all three indices is trading below their gamma flip levels, meaning dealers are short gamma and will amplify moves rather than dampen them.
macro_drivers: US strikes on Iranian rocket launchers near Strait of Hormuz on Sunday spark futures selloff and oil surge
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech keeps rate-hike bets elevated, pressuring stocks and lifting yields
September rate-hike odds have jumped sharply
S&P 500 futures fall as risk-off tone spreads from Middle East escalation and hawkish Fed rhetoric compounding Friday's losses
Dollar and oil strength persist as traders digest hawkish Fed signals alongside geopolitical risk
VIX remains near 2026 lows but seasonal volatility pickup and Middle East risk cloud sentiment
